title: Chevron Richmond refinery fire: sulfidation corrosion, recommendation-tracking gaps, and hard-data proof burden
summary: Chevron Richmond is encoded as a process-safety barrier-health and proof-burden record: known damage mechanisms, low-silicon carbon-steel variability, inspection-data conventions, informal recommendation tracking, and turnaround screening shaped whether a vulnerable pipe component was replaced before rupture.

status_history.note: Added as process-safety / CSB lane record.

subjects.name: high-temperature sulfidation corrosion of carbon-steel piping
U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board

claims.claim: The CSB news release states that missed opportunities to apply inherently safer design, failure to identify/evaluate damage-mechanism hazards, and lack of effective safeguards culminated in the vapor-cloud release and fire at the Chevron Richmond refinery on August 6, 2012.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The same CSB release says the hydrocarbon release endangered 19 workers who narrowly escaped before ignition, caused a fire plume across the area, and was followed by 15,000 people seeking medical treatment in the weeks after the accident.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The CSB final report says pre-mid-1980s refinery carbon-steel piping can contain varying silicon percentages and experience highly variable sulfidation-corrosion rates; post-incident testing of the failed 4-sidecut circuit found silicon ranging from 0.01 to 0.2 weight percent, and the ruptured 52-inch component had only 0.01 weight percent silicon.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The CSB final report says no formal system was in place at Chevron Richmond to communicate to refinery management and track to completion ETC findings/recommendations, and that an indicators program did not measure implementation status of critical ETC recommendations and new industry guidance.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: For the cube, Chevron Richmond is a barrier-health/proof-burden case: low-silicon piping susceptibility, inspection-data conventions, turnaround work screens, and recommendation-tracking gaps delayed replacement/inspection until after rupture.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

type_payload.incident_class: refinery pipe rupture, vapor-cloud fire, process-safety management failure
type_payload.system: crude unit 4-sidecut piping, damage-mechanism review, inspection data, turnaround work prioritization, recommendation tracking

sequence_of_events.event: Longstanding sulfidation-corrosion susceptibility and low-silicon carbon-steel variability existed in the 4-sidecut circuit.
Recommendations and inspection concerns did not become comprehensive replacement/inspection before the 2012 incident.
A 52-inch pipe component ruptured, releasing high-temperature hydrocarbons and producing a vapor cloud.
The release ignited after workers narrowly escaped, causing fire and community plume exposure.

type_payload.proximate_cause: Rupture of carbon-steel piping thinned by sulfidation corrosion, followed by flammable hydrocarbon release and ignition.
contributing_factors: damage-mechanism hazard review and mechanical-integrity gaps
latent_conditions: legacy refinery components and heterogeneous material properties not fully surfaced by standard CML inspection practices
technical authority burdened with persuading management rather than hazard owning a conservative replacement default
